cut_items.item: Use key={userId} on the component so React resets its state on user change
Missing userId in the dependency array means the effect never re-runs and the old user's data stays permanently
Suggests key={userId} to make React reset the component state on user switch
Checks for a missing userId in the dependency array, which would cause the effect not to re-run and show the old user's data
Guidance on when to choose the abort approach versus the flag (use the flag if the fetch library cannot abort)

added_items.item: React cleanup does not cancel a fetch by itself; the code must ignore the stale response
React Strict Mode runs effects twice in development, producing duplicate requests without cleanup
Explicit note that an aborted fetch rejects with AbortError and must be filtered out or it shows as a real error (X's code handles it but does not explain it)
Explains that cleanup runs on userId change but cannot cancel a fetch by itself, so code must ignore stale responses
Mentions React Strict Mode double-running effects in development, causing duplicate requests without cleanup
